title: Official Darts Rules, Dimensions, Formats & Scoring Specifications

authoritative_sources.tournament_format: PDC Tournament Rules & World Darts Championship Regulations

general_dra_rules.scope: Universal standards applied across all sanctioned professional darts competitions globally (PDC, WDF, and affiliated leagues).

world_championship_specific_format.scope: Tournament-specific match structures and rules exclusive to the PDC World Darts Championship at Alexandra Palace.
includes: Sets and Legs match structure (first to 3 legs per set)
Round-by-round set distances (Best of 5 up to Best of 13)
Deciding-set two clear legs tiebreak rule (up to 5-5)
Sudden-death 11th leg in deciding sets with pre-leg bull-off

bullseye_height.measured_from: Floor level to the center of the inner bullseye

oche_distance.measured_from: Front face of the dartboard to the back edge of the raised oche (throwline)

diagonal_distance.measured_from: Center of the bullseye to the back of the oche throwline

board_specifications.board_type: Standard 18-inch English sisal bristle board with ultra-thin blade wiring (spider)

scoring_values.inner_bull: 50 points (Red center, counts as double 25 for checkouts)

501_core_rules.turn_format: Each player throws three darts per turn in alternating turns
501_core_rules.finishing_requirement: Exact zero required on a double ring or the 50-point inner bullseye (Double-Out)
501_core_rules.bust_rule: If a player scores more points than required, scores exact 501 without hitting a double, or leaves a score of 1, the turn is 'Bust' and their score resets to what it was at the beginning of that turn

world_championship_format.match_structure: Sets and Legs format (unique to the World Championship and World Grand Prix in the modern PDC)
world_championship_format.leg_requirement: First player to win 3 legs wins the set (Best of 5 legs per set)

tiebreak_rule.rule: Two Clear Legs in Final Set
tiebreak_rule.description: In the deciding set of any match, a player must win by two clear legs (e.g. 3-1, 4-2, 5-3) up to a maximum of 5-5. If the score reaches 5-5 in the deciding set, a sudden-death 11th leg is played, with the player who won the pre-match bull throw deciding who throws first.

averages_calculation.first_9_average: Calculates scoring rate strictly on the first 9 darts of each leg (before finishing attempts pull the scoring average down)
averages_calculation.tactical_implication: A higher 3-dart average does not guarantee victory because darts is won on legs and sets. If Player A wins their sets 3-0 while Player B edges long 3-2 sets, Player B may hit more 180s and register a higher overall average despite losing the match.
